title: The School Festival's Reusable Decorations
passage:
Every autumn, classes at Nishioka School decorated hallways for the school festival. Colorful paper arches, signs, stars, and hanging shapes appeared for two days and were then removed. Most decorations were made quickly and thrown away afterward. The art club began wondering whether the school could reduce this waste without making every year's festival look the same.

Their first idea was to save all decorations. That failed immediately. Some paper pieces were torn during removal, and storing large three-dimensional objects required more space than the school had. Teachers also pointed out that students valued designing something new each year. Reuse could not simply mean keeping everything unchanged.

The club changed the question. Instead of asking which finished decorations could be reused, they asked which parts could become materials for future designs. They built a set of lightweight wooden frames in three sizes. Classes could cover the frames with paper, cloth, string, or cardboard to create arches, signs, or display walls. At the end of the festival, the temporary surface materials could be removed while the frames remained.

They also created boxes of reusable clips, hooks, and colored cords. Previously, classes had attached decorations with large amounts of tape. The tape was difficult to remove and often damaged both walls and paper. Clips took longer to plan around, but they allowed materials to be separated and saved.

The first year was imperfect. Some students felt restricted by the standard frame sizes. One class wanted a curved entrance that the rectangular frames could not create. Rather than force all classes to use the system, the club made reuse optional and asked participants to report what was difficult. After the festival, they added two flexible frame pieces and more attachment points.

The second year, almost two thirds of the classes used at least one reusable component. The hallways did not look identical because each class covered and combined the frames differently. Storage space was needed, but the frames stacked flat against one wall of a supply room. The school bought less cardboard and tape, and cleanup was faster.

The art club realized that reuse works best when it preserves creativity rather than replacing it. A finished decoration carries one design, but a reusable structure can support many designs. They had shifted from saving objects to saving useful possibilities. This idea later influenced other events. The music club reused stage platforms with different covers, and the science club stored display stands separately from posters. Sustainability became less about keeping old things exactly as they were and more about designing parts that could return in new forms.
translation:
西岡中学校では毎秋の文化祭で、廊下に紙のアーチや看板、星形の飾りなどを大量に作り、二日後には多くを捨てていました。美術部は、毎年同じ見た目にせず、ごみを減らせないか考えました。

最初は完成した飾りを全部保存しようとしましたが、外すと破れる紙も多く、大型の立体飾りを保管する場所もありません。さらに、毎年新しいものを作ること自体が文化祭の楽しみだという意見もありました。

そこで問いを変え、完成品ではなく『次回の材料になる部分』を残すことにしました。三種類の大きさの軽い木製フレームを作り、紙、布、ひも、段ボールなどをかぶせれば、アーチ、看板、展示壁など様々に使えるようにしました。祭り後は表面だけ外し、骨組みは残します。

再利用できるクリップ、フック、色ひもの箱も用意しました。それまで大量に使っていたテープは壁や紙を傷め、材料を分けて残すのが難しかったからです。

初年度には、決まった枠の大きさが創作を制限すると感じる生徒もいました。曲線の入口を作りたいクラスもありました。そこで使用を強制せず、困った点を集め、次年度には曲げられる部品や取り付け場所を増やしました。

二年目には約三分の二のクラスが何らかの再利用部品を使いましたが、表面や組み合わせが違うため廊下は同じ見た目にはなりませんでした。フレームは平らに重ねて倉庫の壁際へ収納でき、段ボールやテープの購入量も減り、片付けも速くなりました。

美術部は、再利用は創造性をなくすのではなく、創造性を支える形にすると成功しやすいと学びました。完成した飾りは一つのデザインしか持ちませんが、再利用可能な構造は多くのデザインを支えられます。『古い物をそのまま残す』のではなく、『別の形で戻ってこられる部品を設計する』ことが持続可能性につながったのです。
